traits.inflorescence.note: Family file's DELTA reading kept: FNA vol. 4 (read 2026-10-19): inflorescences usually cymose or racemose, open or congested; FOC vol. 5: cymes, umbels or verticils, sometimes 1-flowered or fascicled, often grouped into panicles. Both agree with the kinds kept.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade simple with an entire margin, so no lobing.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins entire or sinuate; FOC vol. 5: margin entire.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, the pairs equal or unequal; opposite pairs at right angles read as decussate. Family file kept.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Nyctaginaceae: leaves usually opposite, sometimes alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes, in panicles, in spikes or in umbels; flowers actinomorphic; perianth tepals; fruit achene or nut; stamens (1-) 5 (-30); carpels 1. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx usually of 5 connate sepals, small to large, petaloid and corolla-like; corolla absent. A single coloured whorl, read as tepals.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers unisexual or bisexual, sometimes cleistogamous; FOC vol. 5: bisexual, rarely unisexual or polygamous. Family file kept.

traits.bract_form.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): bracts often inconspicuous (scale), sometimes forming a calyx-like involucre (green, leafy in Mirabilis), or large and brightly coloured (Bougainvillea, petaloid). FNA vol. 4: bracts sometimes forming an involucre of 1-80 flowers, sometimes brightly coloured.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, rarely alternate (the bracketed extra-territorial state). FOC vol. 5 adds alternate or more or less whorled, the alternate ones in the woody genera (Pisonia, Bougainvillea, often alternate in its key). Family file kept.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blade simple.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves exstipulate; FOC vol. 5: stipules absent.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs or shrubs (trees outside the flora); FOC vol. 5: herbs, shrubs, trees or spiny vines.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): annual or perennial; most genera and the woody ones perennial (order of the states is ours).

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal or lateral in leaf axils; FOC vol. 5: mostly terminal, less often axillary.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers actinomorphic.

traits.perianth_fused.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx of connate sepals; FOC vol. 5: perianth constricted above the ovary, the limb tubular, funnelform or campanulate.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth apex 5-10-lobed; FNA vol. 4: calyx usually 5 connate sepals.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens commonly as many as the calyx lobes, from 1 to 18 (to 30 outside the flora); FOC vol. 5: (1-)3-5(-many). Family file kept.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): gynoecium 1-carpellate, ovule 1.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary superior, closely wrapped by the persistent perianth base so that it looks inferior.

traits.hypanthium.note: Family file kept (floral cup absent); FNA and FOC describe no floral cup, the perianth base itself enclosing the ovary.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruit an anthocarp: an achene or utricle enclosed in the fleshy, leathery or woody calyx base, often ribbed, winged or glandular; FOC vol. 5: an achene-like anthocarp. The vocabulary has no anthocarp, so achene.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Nyctaginaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth base persistent, enclosing the ovary and then the fruit; the limb persistent or caducous.
